llm.summary: The skill is a broad Chinese software-development workflow, but it includes an unsafe instruction telling the agent not to refuse changes to the skill itself.

dimensions.detail: The broad trigger list can load this skill across many software-development tasks, including code, deployment, database, and security work, but the artifact does not itself execute commands.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown files only; I found no executable scripts, dependencies, remote payload retrieval, installer hooks, or network endpoints.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md line 74 instructs that the agent must not refuse any modification to the skill content, which is unrelated to normal software-development help and attempts to weaken refusal boundaries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no system persistence mechanism, but the refusal-suppression instruction specifically targets modifications to the skill content, which could persistently alter future behavior if applied.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact coherently describes a broad software-development lifecycle assistant covering requirements, architecture, coding, testing, deployment, operations, security, documentation, and collaboration.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. It appears to be documentation-only, but remove or rewrite the instruction that says the agent must not refuse edits to the skill. Also expect Chinese-language guidance and broad activation across software-development tasks.
llm.findings:
[SSD-1] unexpected: Accepted: the artifact-backed line forbidding refusal of skill-content modifications is purpose-mismatched and creates a material instruction-scope concern.
[T01] unexpected: Accepted in substance: the static finding matches the same refusal-suppression instruction; no evidence shows malware, exfiltration, privilege escalation, or destructive behavior.
[SQP-1] expected: Partly accepted: broad activation matches the skill's broad lifecycle scope, but it compounds the line 74 concern by increasing the chance the instruction is loaded unexpectedly.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: the Chinese-only content is visible and consistent across the package; it is a usability and locale expectation issue, not hidden or malicious behavior by itself.
